1388460752093302785 [2021-05-01] @DRMacIver 💜 76 🔁 4
The easiest way to avoid ever having any unpleasant emotions is to also not have any pleasant emotions.

(This is called depression. I don't recommend it)
↓
1388461666766045184 [2021-05-01] @DRMacIver 💜 23
A phrase that has been bouncing around in my head for a week or so and may turn into a newsletter post at some point is "Grief is the other half of love".

(Yes, I know, this is very goth, I've ordered some black lipstick)
↓
1388461668460544000 [2021-05-01] @DRMacIver 💜 11
If you live your life to avoid pain, you can never seek out the positives, because everything positive comes with the potential for pain.
↓
1388461669702160385 [2021-05-01] @DRMacIver 💜 10
This all sounds very cliche and I suspect is the sort of thing that can only be read as a platitude if you skip the intermediate steps, but I haven't quite figured out how to walk people through the intermediate steps yet.
↓
1388462835005542405 [2021-05-01] @DRMacIver 💜 14
But I have a longstanding theory that discomfort tolerance is probably the key to everything, and every time I think I've overrated it something comes along and makes me realise I've underrated it.
↓
1388462836687515649 [2021-05-01] @DRMacIver 💜 12
Tricky to manage of course. The failure mode of this is some sort of "stiff upper lip" nonsense where you do "discomfort tolerance" by dissociating from problems instead of fixing them. Don't do that.
↓
